commands.goal: Name the adapter one aggregate answers one verb through
commands.name: Bind

aggregates.description: One aggregate-to-adapter binding inside a hecksagon — the verb it answers, the adapter it names. Its own root because a hecksagon's binds are an open set of verbs (one per declared port), which no value object can hold — the same reasoning Wiring carries for a world's settings.
aggregates.name: AdapterBinding

aggregates.description: A primary port — the boundary between a domain and its adapters, in hexagonal terms, is exactly what a hecksagon already IS for every other port. Root-level (belongs to the chapter) or aggregate-scoped (reached the same way persisted_by is, through the open Const.verb(...) door). One of two shapes, never both: a list of operations translating an inbound fact into this domain's own events, or a bare verb naming a swappable resource port (the same Hecks.port a project's own .port file declares, reached from inside the hecksagon instead).
aggregates.name: DomainPort

invariants.description: an answer names a real method

commands.goal: Open a hecksagon for a domain
commands.name: Declare

commands.goal: Take a hecksagon's own event, from outside the domain's own bluebook
commands.name: Subscribe

commands.goal: Attach a framework/bluebook/ member to this hecksagon
commands.name: UsesFramework

commands.goal: Attach a vendored, external bluebook to this hecksagon
commands.name: UsesEmbryonautBluebook

aggregates.description: One .hecksagon — the events a domain subscribes to, and the root every binding hangs off. A sibling artifact to the bluebook, not part of it.
aggregates.name: Hecksagon

aggregates.description: One operation a port exposes — the same shape a command's payload has (attributes in, an event out) with none of a command's given/ensures/sets : a port operation is the translation boundary itself, not a second place business rules live. Those stay on whichever command a policy triggers in reaction to the event it emits.
aggregates.name: PortOperation
